page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highcpu-1 is an arm64-based virtual machine instance belonging to the n4a server family. It features 1 dedicated vCPU and 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance does not include any bundled local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

This instance is designed for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation with a minimal memory footprint. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio represents a compute-focused configuration within a low-resource tier. The absence of local storage and GPU accelerators limits its utility to stateless, non-graphical applications. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated arm64 architecture provides a predictable execution environment for lightweight tasks without the overhead of larger multi-core systems.

Appropriate workloads for the n4a-highcpu-1 instance include lightweight microservices, simple web serving, task queue workers, and basic CI/CD pipeline runners that do not require extensive memory or local disk caching.
